meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

provisions.textEn:
Official language and the right to an interpreter


(3) Parties and subjects in the proceedings who do not speak or understand the Romanian language shall be provided, free of charge, with the possibility to learn of the evidence in the case, to speak and to argue in court, using an interpreter. In the situations where legal assistance is mandatory, the suspect or accused person shall be provided, free of charge, with the possibility to communicate via an interpreter with their counsel so as to prepare the hearing, the filing of an avenue of appeals, or any other motion that has to do with the resolution of the case.

(4) Authorised interpreters are used in the judicial proceedings, according to the law. They are included in the category of interpreters and authorised translators, according to the law.

provisions.comment: Altough no reference was explicitly made to Directive 2010/64/EU within the body of the Law, the Explanatory memorandum mentioned that the provision of Law no. 255/2013 transpose in national legislation the following: Article 1, Article 2 para. 1-5, Article 3 para 1, 2, 7 and 9 and Article 4 from the Directive.
provisions.textEn:
In Article 12, para. 3 is amended and shall have the following content:


“(3) Parties and subjects in the proceedings who do not speak or understand the Romanian language shall be provided, free of charge, with the possibility to learn of the evidence in the case, to speak and to argue in court, using an interpreter. In the situations where legal assistance is mandatory, the suspect or defendant shall be provided, free of charge, with the possibility to communicate via an interpreter with their counsel so as to prepare the hearing, the filing of an avenue of appeals, or any other motion that has to do with the resolution of the case.”.

This law transposes provisions contained in European Union directives, as follows:

Article 1 para. 1, Article 2 para. 1 - 5, Article 3 para. 1, 2, 5, 7 and 9 and Article 4 of Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings, published in the Official Journal of the European Union (JOUE), series L, no. 280 of October 26, 2010.

Use of the native language and the interpreter in court

 

(1) The judicial procedure shall be conducted in Romanian.

(2) Romanian citizens belonging to national minorities have the right to express themselves in the native language before the courts, under the conditions of the organic law.

(3) The modalities of exercising the right provided for in para. 2, including through the use of interpreters or translations, shall be established in such a way as not to impede the proper administration of justice and not to involve additional expenses for those interested.

(4) Foreign citizens and stateless persons who do not understand or speak the Romanian language have the right to become aware of all the acts and proceedings of the file, to speak and to argue in court, through an interpreter; in criminal cases this right is provided free of charge.

nationalActs.title: Lege nr. 304/2004 privind organizarea judiciară
nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 304 from 28 June 2004 regarding the judicial organisation

provisions.textEn:
(1) The judicial procedure shall be conducted in Romanian.

(2) The Romanian citizens belonging to the national minorities have the right to express themselves in their native language, before the courts, under the conditions of the present law.

(3) If one or more parties request to speak in their native language, the court shall ensure, free of charge, the use of an authorized interpreter or translator.

(4) In case all the parties request or agree to speak in their native language, the court must ensure the exercise of this right, as well as the good administration of justice, respecting the principles of contradictory, oral and publicity.

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.
items.comment: Article 318 CCP regulates the waiver of prosecution solution. This can be decided by the public prosecutor in cases where the law stipulates the penalty of the fine or the punishment of imprisonment for a maximum of 7 years, and when there is no public interest in the prosecution. The solution of the prosecutor must be checked for both legality and opportunity by the preliminary chamber judge (see Article 318 para. 12 et seq., amended by Emergency Ordinance no. 18/2016, following decision no. 23/2016 of the Constitutional Court). Therefore, in front of the court (in this case the preliminary chamber judge), the general standards apply.

items.text: 4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.
items.comment:
According to the CCP, the legal counsel of the suspect / accused person has access to all stages of the criminal proceedings.

Few exceptions are regulated by Article 92 para. 1 letters a) and b): cases in which the special methods of supervision or research (provided for in chap. IV of Title IV CCP) are used or in the situation of bodily or vehicle searches in the case of flagrant offenses.


In addition, access to the case file is generally available and can be restricted by the public prosecutor (Article 94 para. 5) only during the investigation phase (the so called urmărire penală in Romanian law). If the person has already the status of accused perspn (e.g., the criminal action commenced, being triggered by the prosecutor), the restriction can be imposed for a maximum of up to 10 days.

items.heading: Article 2
items.comment: The final part of Law no. 255/2013 explicitly mentions that the amendments brought to the CCP transposed inter alia the provisions of Article 2 para. 1-5 from this Directive. Still, we consider that we are in the presence of an indirect implementation, as Law no. 255 did not bring actual novelty in this field.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

provisions.textEn:
Questions regarding the person of the suspect or the accused person


(1) At the beginning of the first hearing, the judicial body asks questions to the suspect or the accused person regarding the name, surname, nickname, date and place of birth, personal numeric code, parents' names and surnames, citizenship, marital status, military situation, studies, profession or occupation, place of employment, domicile and address where he or she actually resides and the address at which he / she wish for procedural documents to be communicated, criminal records or if another criminal case is being held against him, if he asks for an interpreter if he does not speak or not understands the Romanian language or cannot express it, as well as on any other data for establishing his personal situation.

(2) The questions provided in para. (1) shall be repeated at subsequent hearings only when the judicial body deems it necessary.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that, where necessary for the purpose of safeguarding the fairness of the proceedings, interpretation is available for communication between suspected or accused persons and their legal counsel in direct connection with any questioning or hearing during the proceedings or with the lodging of an appeal or other procedural applications.

provisions.comment:
Romanian law provides the free of charge interpreter in order to facilitate the communication with the legal counsel only in cases where legal assistance is mandatory. These cases are regulater by Article 90 and 91 CPP.

In all other cases the use of an interpreter for the communcations between the legal counsel and his client (suspect / accused) is of course, permited, but the suspect or accused must bear the costs, as the state has no involvement.
provisions.textEn:
Official language and the right to an interpreter


(3) In the situations where legal assistance is mandatory, the suspect or accused person shall be provided, free of charge, with the possibility to communicate via an interpreter with their counsel so as to prepare the hearing, the filing of an avenue of appeals, or any other motion that has to do with the resolution of the case.

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

provisions.textEn:
Hearing with the help of an interpreter


(3) If the person heard is deaf, mute or deaf and mute, the hearing is done with the participation of a person who has the ability to communicate through the special language. In this situation, communication can also be done in writing.

(4) In exceptional cases, if there is not an authorised person who can communicate through the special language, and the communication cannot be made in writing, the hearing of the persons mentioned in para. (3) will be made with the help of any person who has communication skills, the provisions of para. (2) applying properly.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

provisions.textEn:
Hearing with the help of an interpreter


(1) Whenever the audited person does not understand, speak or speak well in Romanian, the hearing is done through an interpreter. The interpreter may be appointed by the judicial bodies or chosen by the parties or the injured person, from the authorized interpreters, according to the law.

(2) Exceptionally, in the case of the urgent need for a procedural measure or if an authorized interpreter cannot be provided, the hearing may take place in the presence of any person who can communicate with the listener, but the judicial body is obliged to to resume the hearing by the interpreter as soon as possible.

(1) At the beginning of the first hearing, the judicial body asks questions to the suspect or the accused person regarding the name, surname, nickname, date and place of birth, personal numeric code, parents' names and surnames, citizenship, marital status, military situation, studies, profession or occupation, place of employment, domicile and address where he or she actually resides and the address at which he / she wishes to be communicated the procedural documents, criminal records or if another criminal case is being held against him, if he asks for an interpreter if he does not speak or not understands the Romanian language or cannot express it, as well as on any other data for establishing his personal situation

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.
items.comment: There is no specific means of challenging such a decision so no interlocutory appeal is granted. The general right to challenge a decision together with the judgment per se, as granted by the CCP, is applicable - namely appeal (in case of judgment on the merits) or challenge - contestatie in Romanian (in all other cases, e.g., rullings on preventive detention, preliminary chamber rulings, etc.).

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

In urgent cases, technical means of communication may be used, if it is considered necessary and does not impede the exercise of the rights of the injured person.

items.comment:
Such a specific provision exists only in the case of the injured party - Article 81 letter g-1 CCP.


In general, the CCP prefers the replacement of the interpreter with other person who can communicate / speak that language - see Article 105 para. 2 CCP.


The CCP mentions the possibility of video conference but the hypothesis refers to the case where the physical presence of the accused person is not possible (e.g., he is in held in custody) be present. In this case, the legal counsel and the interpreter are physically present.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents
items.comment: The final part of Law no. 255/2013 states that Article 3 para. 1, 2, 5 and 7 were transposed by the CCP, as amended by this law. We are, in fact, in the presence of a partial (and incomplete) transposition.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn:
Referral to the court


(3) In case the accused person does not know the Romanian language, measures will be taken for the authorised translation of the indictment, which will be attached to the documents mentioned in para. (2). When there are no authorised translators, the translation of the indictment is done by a person who can communicate with the accused person.

(4) The accused person, a Romanian citizen belonging to a national minority, may request that a translation of the indictment be communicated in his / her native language.

Use of native language and the interpreter in court


(1) The judicial procedure is conducted in Romanian language.

(2) Romanian citizens belonging to national minorities have the right to express themselves in their native language before the courts, under the conditions of the organic law.

(3) The modalities of exercising the right provided for in para. 2, including through the use of interpreters or translations, shall be established in such a way as not to impede the proper administration of justice and not to involve additional expenses for those interested.

(4) Foreign citizens and stateless persons who do not understand or speak the Romanian language have the right to become aware of all the acts and proceedings of the file, to speak in court and to draw conclusions, through an interpreter; in criminal cases this right is provided free of charge.

items.comment: As we will show, although the CCP mentions only a written translation of the indictment, there are several other provisions that grant that oral / verbal translation is provided. As well, the Constitution makes reference to the right to become aware of all the acts and proceedings of the file.

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.
items.comment: Article 329 para. 3 and 4 CCP makes reference only to the indictment act.

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.
items.comment: There is no explicit obligation / duty on authorities to translate any other document, besides the indicment. The suspect or accused is enttield to submit any request, including the one mentioned here by Article 3 para. 3 from the Directive - see Article 92 para. 4 CCP.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.
items.comment: There is no explicit obligation / duty on authorities to translate any other document, besides the indicment

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.
items.comment: There is no specific means of challenging such a decision so no interlocutory appeal is granted. The general right to challenge a decision together with the judgment per se, as granted by the CCP, is applicable - namely appeal (in case of judgment of the merits) or contestation (in all other cases, e.g., rullings on preventive detention, preliminary chamber rulings, etc.).

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

There are several other cases where the CCP provides that the suspect or accused person must be informed, in the language, he / she understands. items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.

a) the person concerned did not invoke it within the term provided by law;

items.comment: There is no waiver regulated, but the general principles of the CCP can be applied, as this is a right granted to the suspect and accused. Violating this right by the judicial organs leads to a serious breach to the right to a fair trial and, hence, the conditions of Article 282 CCP (relative nullity) are incident. According to Article 282 para. 5 CCP the relative nullity (or relative invalidity) is covered when the person concerned did not invoke it within the term provided by law or it expressly renounced the invocation of invalidity

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

(1) The Ministry of Justice draws up the lists with the authorized interpreters and translators, as well as with those provided in art. 61 paragraph (4), which it communicates to the Superior Council of Magistracy, the High Court of Cassation and Justice, the Prosecutor's Office attached to the High Court of Cassation and Justice, the National Anticorruption Prosecutor's Office and the courts of appeal.

(2) The Prosecutor's Office attached to the High Court of Cassation and Justice shall communicate the lists with the interpreters and translators authorized to the subordinate prosecutor's offices.

(3) The courts of appeal shall forward these lists to the courts and tribunals in their constituencies.

 

(4) The lists shall also be communicated to the Ministry of Administration and Interior, to the National Union of Notaries Public, to the National Union of Bars in Romania and to the National Union of Judicial Executors, who will inform the subordinate criminal investigation bodies, as the case may be. , the offices of notaries public, the law firms and the offices of judicial executors.

(5) Updating the lists provided in par. (1) - (4) will be done periodically, depending on the authorization of new persons or the termination of the quality of interpreter or authorized translator.

(1) The interpreters and translators authorized under the conditions of this law are obliged to request, within 60 days from the date of the authorization, the record in the court in the district in which they reside.

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

provisions.textEn: Authorized interpreters and translators have the obligation to respect the confidentiality of the facts, information and documents that they become aware of in the exercise of the activity, both during the holding of the quality and after its termination, unless the law or the party interested in maintaining its confidentiality release from this obligation.

items.comment: Law no. 178/1997 was amended by Law no. 76/2016, which explicitly provides that is transposes Arrticle 5 para. 1 and 3 from the Directive.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.

items.comment: Although the EJN website identifies at the transposition level in Romanian law several Regulations adopted by the Romanian Superior Council of Magistrates and the National Institute for Magistrates, there is no explicit provisions regarding such training. Best case scenario, it can be included in the general good organization of the hearing in court actually takes place (the assistance of an interpreter being thus included). In addition, there are several guides drafted in order to facilitate the communication between the judges and the legal counsels and probably general guidelines will be derived from there. These guides are not official yet, as are part of an ongoing project.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.
items.heading: Article 7

provisions.textEn:
Record of statements

 

(4) The written declaration shall be signed by the criminal prosecution body which proceeded to the hearing of the suspect or the accused person, the judge of rights and freedoms or the president of the trial and clerk's court, the lawyer of the suspect or of the accused person, the injured person, the civil party or the civilly responsible party, if they were present, as well as the interpreter when the declaration was taken by an interpreter.

 

(5) During the criminal prosecution, the hearing of the suspect or the accused person shall be recorded by audio or audiovisual technical means. When registration is not possible, this is recorded in the statement of the suspect or the accused person, with the concrete indication of why the registration was not possible.

items.comment:
When an interpreter is used, he will sign as well every each page of the declaration. As well, the presence and help of the interpreter will be noted by the police officer or public prosecutor in a minute (proces-verbal) and by the court in a resolution or in its final judgment (if this event occurred in the last session).

There is a general obligation to record (video or audio) every aspect and element of the trial. This is always the case in court (generally audio), but in during the investigative, due to the lack of infrastructure, such recordings will be exceptional. When recording is not possible, the police officer or prosecutor will note this in a minute, as well.

Regarding waiver or the usage of an oral translation, the investigative authority or public prosecutor will note this in a minute, while the court will do so in a resolution or the final judgment (if this event occurred in the last session).
